historical_references.reference: Surur is an epithet given to the Islamic Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) in the Quran, meaning 'gentle' or 'subtle'. It is used in verse 57:26 as a description of Allah's ability to 'soothe' the hearts of His believers and grant them victory.

The Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid I (685-715 CE) is known to have built the Dome of the Rock in Jerusalem, which was the first major Islamic structure dedicated to worship. The name 'Surur' is inscribed on the exterior of the Dome, possibly as a reference to the Prophet Muhammad's gentle and calming influence over his followers and over the land of Palestine.
